The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) disclosed this in a post on its verified X handle on Tuesday.
The commission said the judgment was delivered by Justice Ismail Ijelu following a trial over the unauthorised withdrawal of ₦1 million from an account belonging to Leelee Dumbari.
According to the EFCC, investigations revealed that Nweke, on June 21, 2025, in Lagos, accessed a desktop computer assigned to one Emmanuella Anyanwu without lawful authority, thereby facilitating the unauthorised withdrawal.
The offence is contrary to Section 386(1) of the Criminal Law of Lagos State, 2011.
Following the investigation, the EFCC’s Lagos Zonal Directorate 1 arraigned Nweke on a one-count charge bordering on the unlawful withdrawal of ₦1 million from Dumbari’s account domiciled with a new-generation bank.
Nweke pleaded not guilty to the charge, prompting a full trial.
During the proceedings, prosecution counsel, M.K. Bashir, called five witnesses to establish the case against the defendant, while the defence called one witness.
Delivering judgment, Justice Ijelu found Nweke guilty as charged and ordered him to pay a fine of ₦1 million within 30 days.
The court further ruled that failure to pay the fine within the stipulated period would result in his remand in a correctional centre for six months.
